title: Update the Mustang wiring
goal: Remove the accessory wiring added in high school, fix the factory faults found along the way, and install a fused, relay-switched fuse block so the radio, amp and tach each get their own fused circuit.
summary: The old add-on wiring has been removed and diagnosis of the factory circuits is underway, with the engine out of the car and the ignition switch and headlight switch out of the dash for testing. Found so far: a short to ground on circuit 11 (passenger front parking light), a turn-signal fault in the switch or its blue-pin connector, a heater fan switch that never grounds, and a loose unidentified solid-red wire at the starter relay. The install sheet is the current set of install steps and supersedes the guide's step-by-step section (which still describes a generic separate relay and a 30 A fuse); the guide's circuit plan, connection methods, parts and shopping list are current.
next_step: Tape over the live blue terminal on the hazard board. Then sort out the driver front light's three wires, replace the blown hazard fuse, and swap-test the turn-signal flasher.

subprojects.title: Finish diagnosing the turn signals
subprojects.goal: Replace the dead turn-signal flasher and get all four corners and both dash arrows working.
subprojects.summary: The factory turn-signal flasher is dead (open circuit). The lever switch, rear wiring, rear bulbs and brake lights are proven good. The four-wire block the earlier tests centered on is the missing hazard switch's terminal board, not part of the turn-signal path. Remaining: confirm with a flasher swap, then replace the flasher.
notes: How it works (1966 factory diagrams): there are two flashers. The hazard flasher is always hot (battery → fuse → orange feed) → blue → hazard switch board. The turn-signal flasher is hot with the key on (ignition accessory 297 → orange-yellow 8) → blue (44) → the lever switch's own plug at the column base.

Lever switch: neutral = flasher input connected to nothing, brake feeds both rears. Left = flasher to left front + left rear, brake to right rear. Right = flasher to right front + right rear, brake to left rear.

Wire colors: front turn green-white = left (driver), white-blue = right (passenger); brake green-red; rears orange-blue (5) and green-orange (9) on the two-wire plug. Each front light also has a parking wire and a black ground.
Corrected 2026-11-14: earlier notes treated the four-wire block as the turn-signal switch connector and the hazard flasher as the turn-signal flasher. Both were wrong.

tasks.text: Switch-side continuity test: both switch plugs unplugged, battery off; blue to each front/rear pin with lever left, right, neutral
tasks.detail: Done 2026-11-13 on the lever switch's own six-wire and two-wire plugs: blue switches to the correct front and rear with the lever, and the brake feed reaches both rears in neutral. The old 'four-wire connector' turned out to be the hazard switch board, so this test as written no longer applies.

tasks.text: If the switch passes: inspect, clean and re-seat the blue (44) pin in both halves of the four-wire connector
tasks.detail: Not needed: the four-wire block is the hazard switch's terminal board, not part of the turn-signal path.

tasks.text: If the switch fails: replace the turn-signal switch (steering wheel removal required)
tasks.detail: Not needed: the lever switch tested good (continuity and back-feed jumper tests).

tasks.text: Explain why the flasher has 12 V with the key OFF (should be fed from accessory circuit 297)
tasks.detail: Answered: the flasher with 12 V key-off is the hazard flasher, which is meant to be always hot.

tasks.text: Identify the driver front light's three wires before reconnecting (turn = green-white, ground = black, third = parking); fix any swap made during testing
tasks.detail: The driver front blinked with the hazard-corner (green-red) jumper, which suggests a miswire there if the lever was in neutral.

tasks.text: Replace the blown hazard-circuit fuse (only after the driver front wires are sorted), then confirm the hazard flasher's orange feed has power
tasks.detail: It blew when wires were swapped at the driver front light while live. Replacing it first risks blowing it again.

tasks.text: Key on: test light on each terminal of the turn-signal flasher's socket; one should light (orange-yellow 8)
tasks.detail: If neither lights, trace the feed back toward the ignition switch accessory circuit (297) and the fuses.

tasks.text: Swap test: plug the good hazard flasher into the turn-signal flasher's socket, all four bulbs connected; pull the lever left and right
Install a new turn-signal flasher and put the hazard flasher back in its own socket
tasks.detail: Buy after the swap test works. Match the number stamped on the old unit.

tasks.text: Final check: all four corners and both dash arrows; lever left, right and neutral; with and without the brake pressed
Only if something's still off: recheck the green-red jumper at the hazard board with the lever in a turn position (one rear or both?)
tasks.detail: The diagram predicts only one rear; the owner saw both. Low priority.

tasks.text: Reconnect both front parking/turn connectors and test all four corners plus the dash indicator

subprojects.title: Restore the emergency flasher (hazard) switch
subprojects.goal: Working hazards: all four corners flash with the key off.
subprojects.summary: Optional, and separate from the turn signals. The car has the 1965–66 emergency-flasher system: its own flasher, an always-hot feed, and a four-terminal board spliced into the lever switch's wires. The toggle switch that mounts on the board is missing.
notes: Board terminals: blue = hazard flasher output (in). Green-white, white-blue and green-red are spliced into the lever switch's left front, right front and brake wires. The switch connects blue to all three at once.
Ford changed the switch on Mar 1, 1966: before that, a switch on a wiring board; after, a plug-in switch with blade terminals. This board looks like the earlier type.

tasks.text: Safety, do now: tape over or cap the exposed blue terminal on the hazard board (always hot and blinking)
Read the build date on the door data plate (before or after Mar 1, 1966?)
Find a switch that fits the existing four-terminal board; confirm fitment before buying
tasks.detail: Options: NOS C5AZ-15B590-B (seen on eBay); reproduction kits from CJ Pony Parts (EFS1 / EFS2 / EFS3), Scott Drake and Mac's.

tasks.text: Mount the switch (originally in the glove box), connect it, and test hazards with the key off; pressing the brake should make the rears go solid

subprojects.title: Repair or replace the passenger front parking/turn wiring
subprojects.goal: Parking lights work with no crackle and no breaker cycling.
subprojects.summary: Short to ground on circuit 11 (front parking lights) isolated to the passenger-side wiring past the wheel-well connector. It caused the headlight-switch crackle and breaker cycling.
notes: Unplugging the passenger-side wheel-well connector stopped the crackling; unplugging the driver side did not. A crackle at the starter relay was arcing at the relay-bolt ground connection, not the relay switching.

tasks.text: Battery off, bulb out: ohms from wire 11 (light side of the wheel-well connector) to ground; find the exact spot
Inspect socket (melted/corroded/crushed contact) and where the pigtail passes through sheet metal
Repair with splice + heat-shrink + grommet/loom, or replace the socket/pigtail
Check the turn-signal wire in the same socket/pigtail
Reconnect both front lights; confirm park position lights the fronts with no crackle
Clean and tighten the starter-relay mounting bolt ground (it was arcing)
Inspect headlight switch terminals for heat damage; replace the switch if it ever crackles again

subprojects.title: Replace the heater fan switch
subprojects.goal: Heater fan runs on all speeds.
subprojects.summary: Blower motor and resistor work; the factory switch never grounds any output. Fan is ground-side switched on the '66.
notes: Don't run low or medium for long with the resistor outside the heater box; it relies on the blower's airflow for cooling.

tasks.text: Buy a replacement 1966 Mustang heater fan switch
Wire per factory: motor control wire and high-speed wire on the resistor's full-speed terminal, lower speeds on the other taps, switch common to ground
Make sure the switch's ground (housing or ground lead) is on clean bare metal
Test all speeds; keep resistor tests short if it is outside the heater box

subprojects.title: Wire in the fuse block and relay for the accessories
subprojects.goal: Radio, amp and tach each on their own fused, relay-switched circuit.
subprojects.summary: Painless CirKit Boss 70107 under the dash, fed through its breaker from the starter-relay battery stud, triggered from the accessory circuit; radio, amp and tach each on their own fuse.
notes: Follow the install sheet; the guide's step-by-step section (generic relay, 30 A fuse) is superseded. Never take the trigger from the pink coil feed.
2026-11-13: an unused switched 12 V wire under the dash, probably the factory radio feed, plus a three-prong plug that seemed to be for illumination. Details not in the chat export yet.

tasks.text: Buy parts (see shopping-list.csv) and RCA cables
tasks.detail: Bought the Painless kit, wire, connectors, tape and the rest of the list. RCA cables not confirmed.

tasks.text: Identify the unused switched 12 V wire under the dash (probably the factory radio feed): color, which key positions are hot, and which fuse feeds it
tasks.detail: Found during the wiring work. If it is the factory radio feed, it could serve the head unit's switched lead, but the plan runs the radio from the fuse block. Label it or tape it off either way.

tasks.text: Mount the fuse block and ground it
Run the 10 ga feed through a firewall grommet to the kit breaker near the battery
Connect the pink trigger to an ACC+ON circuit (accessory 297) - never the pink coil feed
Wire radio (memory on constant, switched 5 A, illumination to the spare dash-light branch)
Wire tach (3 A ignition circuit, signal to coil -, light to dash-light branch, set to 8 cylinders)
Wire amp (12 ga from a 15 A constant circuit, 12 ga ground under 3 ft, turn-on from radio blue/white)
Run the test sequence on the install sheet
Optional: update the guide doc's install steps to match the Painless kit (the install sheet already does)

subprojects.title: Identify the loose solid-red wire at the starter relay
subprojects.goal: Know what the loose red wire is and where it goes.
subprojects.summary: Comes from the firewall main disconnect with the S, I and battery-stud wires; reads 0 V in every key position; relay end loose.
notes: Don't connect it until identified. The owner believes it used to connect somewhere on the starter relay.

tasks.text: Find its pin and the matching wire color on the cabin side of the main disconnect
Continuity-trace it (battery off) to the ignition switch, fuse panel, headlight switch, flashers, gauges and shifter
Check whether anything in the car is unpowered that should work
Do not connect it until identified

subprojects.title: Engine-out test setup and reinstall electrical checklist
subprojects.goal: Everything restored correctly when the engine goes back in.
subprojects.summary: Temporary setup used for testing with the engine out, and what must be restored when it goes back in.
notes: Coordinate with the engine-302 project: the engine is out and being rebuilt.

tasks.text: Keep the starter cable off the relay (or insulated) while the engine is out; verify its current state
Reconnect the ground cable at the relay mounting bolt to the engine (clean metal both ends)
Restore battery negative to the engine; remove or keep the temporary body ground jumper as an extra ground
Brown back on relay I terminal; main disconnect fully plugged in
Coil +: pink resistance wire and brown/I circuit; check the electronic ignition's voltage requirement first
Coil -: distributor/ignition module wire plus the new tach signal wire
Alternator output wire back on the relay battery stud (if removed); regulator plug connected
Reconnect starter cable last; confirm the relay clicks only in START
Add an engine-to-firewall ground strap if there isn't one

decisions.text: Replace the heater fan switch: the factory switch, with its housing grounded, never grounds any output in any position. (Date approximate.)

Use a fused, relay-switched fuse block (Painless CirKit Boss 70107) triggered from accessory circuit 297, instead of splicing into factory circuits or the starter relay. The install sheet supersedes the guide's generic relay and 30 A fuse steps.
Dropped the 12 V cigarette-lighter socket from the plan.
Don't jump the hazard flasher's blue to the front wires as a fix: the fronts and dash arrows would blink all the time, even key-off, and drain the battery. Replace the turn-signal flasher instead.

open_questions.text: Why do both flasher terminals read 12 V with the key OFF? Per the diagram the flasher is fed from accessory circuit 297.
open_questions.answer: That was the hazard flasher, which is meant to be always hot (battery → fuse → orange feed) so hazards work with the key off.

open_questions.text: What is the loose solid-red wire at the starter relay, and where does it go?
Is the turn-signal fault the switch or the blue (44) pin contact in the four-wire connector?
open_questions.answer: Neither. The four-wire block is the missing hazard switch's terminal board. The lever switch tests good; the turn-signal flasher is dead (open circuit).

open_questions.text: What voltage does the electronic ignition module need on coil +? Check before wiring the coil feed.
Is the amp's onboard blade fuse really red / 10 A?
What is the unused switched 12 V wire under the dash (factory radio feed?), and is the three-prong illumination plug the blue dash-light splitter with the spare branch, or something else?
Is the driver front light miswired? It blinked with the hazard-corner (green-red) jumper; check whether the lever was in neutral.
Was the car built before or after Mar 1, 1966? That decides which hazard switch fits.
